questions.text: I notice that people sometimes wonder if I'm affected by things, but I simply process them at a lower volume.
I tend to take on the overnight shift or the early morning slot so others can have the easier schedule.
I sense the difference between a group that is comfortable with each other and a group that is performing comfort.
I routinely surround myself with people and environments that elevate my personal trajectory.
I forget about other people's suffering as soon as I have something else to think about.
I routinely stay late to help a colleague finish their work, even when mine is already done.
I notice that even subtle shifts in atmosphere — a room going quiet, a change in tone — hit me with force.
I find that I generally miss when someone uses my name mid-conversation to increase intimacy or pressure.
I do not naturally sense when someone wants to be contradicted rather than agreed with.
I routinely gather extra supplies so I can offer them to anyone in my circle who runs short.
I would rather lead a small group than follow in a large one.
When I learn that someone I know is going through a difficult time, my first instinct is rarely to consider how I might help.
I feel more in control when I have a plan, even if it needs to be adjusted later.
I rarely detect when a person's interest in a conversation suddenly spikes because of something specific that was said.
When a friend is hurting, I usually want to help.
Even after hearing only a brief account of someone's suffering, I care what happens to them.
I tend to work on whatever grabs my attention rather than following a priority list.
I enjoy adapting to and reinforcing the culture that already exists on a team.
I often know what someone is about to say before they say it based on context cues.
I find that decorating my space exactly to my taste improves my daily mood and output.
I detect when someone uses a nickname versus a full name to signal the current state of a relationship.
I give others a quick overview and trust them to figure out the details their own way.
I actively lobby for my perspective before a group makes a decision.
I experience the feeling of being startled as a brief flash that dissipates almost immediately.
I establish personal policies for recurring decisions so I don't have to deliberate each time.
I tend to make major life decisions based primarily on what excites and fulfills me.
I find it energizing to be part of a team that navigates challenges together.
I naturally defer to others in informal group settings.
Someone's pain stops mattering to me almost as soon as I stop seeing it.
I tend to feel the emotional stakes of a situation far more intensely than the practical stakes.
When I feel wronged, the indignation is so intense it can keep me awake at night.
I head out the door and figure out what I forgot along the way.
I notice that I can hold space for difficult conversations without my own equilibrium being disrupted.
I use consistent formats and templates for recurring communications.
Another person's hardship pulls at me even when responding is difficult.
I volunteer to chair committees or working groups without hesitation.
